claims.statement: HO-3 edition selection is governed by policy effective date: 2011-05 applies to policies effective before 2018-09-01 under that edition, 2018-09 applies from 2018-09-01 until superseded for policies effective on or after 2024-03-01, and 2024-03 applies from 2024-03-01; superseded editions remain governing for policies written under them.

The 2024 filing memorandum explains the stated rationale for HO-3 2024-03 changes, but the filed form’s agreement and authorized-written-action provisions make the filed form controlling when the memorandum and contract text differ; an attached endorsement controls over inconsistent base-form language only within its stated scope.

Across editions, HO-3 Section I contains Coverages A through D, Additional Coverages, perils, exclusions, and conditions, while Section II contains personal liability and medical payments coverage; the recurring organization does not make the edition-specific grants and exclusions interchangeable.

Coverage B remains 10% of Coverage A and Coverage C remains 50% of Coverage A across the three editions. The 2018 and 2024 forms make their Coverage C special limits subject to the Coverage C limit and other policy terms; the percentage relationships and special-limit treatment must be read from the applicable edition.

Coverage A moves from the 2011 direct-physical-loss and 80%-replacement-cost framework, through the 2018 dwelling, equipment, fixtures, and related direct-loss wording, to the 2024 Declarations-based residence-premises grant with a separate roof-surfacing settlement provision; the 2024 memorandum presents the dwelling, direct-loss, and roof-payment-floor changes as clarifications, while the filed form controls.

Coverage C special limits are edition-specific: 2024 changes the 2018 amounts for cash, jewelry theft, firearms theft, and silverware theft, leaves watercraft, business-property, and electronic-apparatus amounts at their 2018 levels, and the 2011 form states lower amounts for most of those categories.

Coverage D remains 20% of Coverage A, but the operative descriptions differ: 2011 addresses additional living expense and fair rental value after a covered loss makes the premises uninhabitable; 2018 addresses necessary living expenses, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss of use when the premises is unfit; and 2024 details temporary living arrangements, meals, transportation, rental value, moving, storage, and direct causation. The 2024 memorandum says the revision ties loss of use to the applicable covered loss.

Additional Coverages materially change across editions: 2011 provides 5% debris removal, 5% vegetation with a $500 per-item limit, and a $500 fire-department cap; 2018 keeps debris at 5% and raises the latter caps to $750; 2024 raises debris to 10%, vegetation to 10% of Coverage A with a $1,000 per-item cap, and the fire-department cap to $1,000, and adds stated card, assessment, ordinance-or-law, and grave-marker amounts.

The edition-specific water provisions differ: 2011 excludes backup, repeated seepage, subsurface water, and flood including water driven by wind or another force; 2018 expressly covers sudden and accidental system discharge or overflow while excluding repeated seepage and backup; and 2024 separately states accidental discharge, sudden-and-accidental system damage, off-premises plumbing discharge, and flood/surface-water exclusions using the phrase whether water is driven by wind or another force.

The 2024 Section I exclusion lead-in excludes loss caused directly or indirectly by an excluded peril, including concurrent or sequential contribution unless the policy expressly provides otherwise; the memorandum explains the concurrent-cause revision but does not replace that operative text.

The 2024 base form adds a separate roof-surfacing settlement provision and excludes cosmetic wind or hail damage that does not impair water shedding, while HO 23 74 is a separate attached endorsement whose 2018-09 edition applies an actual-cash-value threshold at 15 years and whose later 2025-05 edition applies an actual-cash-value threshold at 12 years or greater. The 2025-05 text also states a 20% payable percentage for an applicable composition-shingle category but later states that covered roof-surfacing payment will not be less than 30% of applicable replacement cost, an apparent internal conflict requiring escalation rather than assumption.

Water-backup and wind or hail percentage-deductible protection are endorsement-dependent rather than automatic base-form coverage: the base forms exclude or limit those causes, while HO 04 90 and HO 23 77 provide edition-specific attached coverage or deductible terms and control only within their stated scope. HO 04 90 2010-10 states a $5,000 limit and $500 deductible; HO 04 90 2027-01 states a $10,000 limit and $1,000 deductible.

The 2024 post-loss conditions require notice, mitigation, preservation and inspection, records and inventory when requested, recovery-right preservation, and a signed sworn proof of loss within 90 days after request; the 2018 form required the sworn proof within 60 days, and the memorandum identifies the 90-day revision.

The 2024 form sets a $500 Section I deductible minimum, provides payment within 60 days after agreement, binding appraisal, or final judgment, and states that appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage, policy interpretation, or compliance.

Section II changes by edition: 2011 provides a compact Coverage E liability grant and three-year Coverage F medical-expense period; 2018 reorganizes Coverage E around defined occurrence, suit, and coverage territory terms and expressly states fault-free Coverage F; 2024 adds on-behalf-of liability wording, personal-activities and separate-insured scope, defense expenses and bond premiums, while retaining no-fault Coverage F and the three-year period.

The 2024 Section II exclusion lead-in expressly includes personal injury and denies a duty to defend claims or suits seeking damages excluded by Section II, whereas the 2011 lead-in addresses bodily injury and property damage without that personal-injury and excluded-defense wording; 2018 sits between them with an expanded exclusion structure.

The 2024 repository form contains apparent duplicated or malformed phrases in DEF.12, Coverage A.13, and certain endorsement cross-references; those textual defects should be flagged or quoted rather than silently corrected, because a filing memorandum cannot rewrite the controlling form.

The 2018-09 filing memorandum is explanatory filing material rather than an additional policy form: it attributes the revision to clarification and alignment of the insuring agreement, definitions, Section I property and limits, exclusions and conditions, Section II liability and medical payments, and editorial organization, while the filed 2018-09 form supplies the operative contract terms.

The filed 2018-09 form states in D.1 that the Coverage D limit is twenty percent of Coverage A. Memorandum item M.3.32 addresses fair rental value for the rented portion of the premises rather than establishing a different percentage limit, so the filed form controls the Coverage D limit.

For the 2018-09 edition, the filed form requires a signed, sworn proof of loss within sixty days after the insurer’s request and limits appraisal to determining the amount of loss rather than coverage or policy interpretation; the memorandum describes those changes as claim-administration clarifications.

The 2018-09 filing memorandum reports a three percent filed rate change and describes renumbering and formatting changes as filing context; those statements do not themselves create Coverage A–F limits, deductibles, exclusions, conditions, or payment obligations.

A state amendatory form is contract language that can supply a precedence rule only for matters within its stated scope, while nonconflicting base-form and endorsement terms remain applicable; it does not provide coverage unless expressly stated. A regulator bulletin instead constrains disclosure and administration and cannot authorize a deductible not permitted by the policy or law.

Endorsement supersession is effective-date-specific: HO 23 74 Actual Cash Value Loss Settlement — Roof Surfacing (Edition 2025-05) supersedes the 2018-09 edition for policies effective on or after 2025-05-01, and HO 04 90 Water Backup and Sump Discharge or Overflow (Edition 2027-01) supersedes the 2010-10 edition for policies effective on or after 2027-01-01; each earlier edition remains in force for policies written under it.
